(''22 March 2014'') | attendance = 1,348,973 | average attendance = '''10,219''' | prevseason = [[2013 Liga Super|2013]] | nextseason = [[2015 Liga Super|2015]] | extra information = All statistics correct as of 28 June 2014. }} The '''2014 Liga Super''' ({{langx|en|'''2014 Super League'''}}), also known as the '''Astro Liga Super''' for sponsorship reasons, is the 11th season of the [[Liga Super]], the top-tier professional [[association football|football]] league in Malaysia.[https://www.rsssf.org/tablesm/malay2014.html] 2014 Liga Super The season was held from 17 January and concluded on 25 June 2014. The [[Liga Super]] champions for 2014 was [[Johor Darul Ta'zim F.C.|Johor Darul Ta'zim]] and this season was the start of them winning the league every season until today. ==Major changes== The following are the key changes of 2014 Liga Super season as compared to the previous season: * The 2014 [[Piala Sumbangsih]] match between [[LionsXII]] and [[Pahang FA|Pahang]] will also be a Liga Super match. Results of the 90-minute match will be counted towards the league table classification. The last time this happened was during the [[2011 Liga Super]] season. * Goal-line referees will be introduced in selected matches during the season, and will be fully implemented for all matches in the [[Liga Super|2015 Liga Super]] season if the feedback is positive.{{cite news |title=Goal line technology |url=http://www.nst.com.my/sports/soccer/goal-line-referees-to-make-debut-in-m-league-1.411229 |work=New Straits Times |date=25 November 2013 |access-date=25 November 2013 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131125094221/http://www.nst.com.my/sports/soccer/goal-line-referees-to-make-debut-in-m-league-1.411229 |archive-date=25 November 2013 |url-status=dead }} * A total of 4 foreign players can be registered by Liga Super teams, including at least one player from [[Asian Football Confederation|AFC]] countries. A maximum of 3 foreign players can be fielded at one time in a match. The announcement was made by FAM during the exco meeting in November 2013, following a decision to upgrade the foreign players quota from 2 in 2013 to 3 in the April 2013 meeting.{{cite news |title=Goal line technology}} ==Team changes== The following teams have changed division. {{col-begin|width=auto}} {{col-break}} ===To Malaysia Super League=== '''Promoted from [[2013 Malaysia Premier League|Premier League]]''' * [[Sarawak FA|Sarawak]] * [[Sime Darby F.C.|Sime Darby]] {{col-break|gap=3em}} ===From Malaysia Super League=== '''Relegated to [[2014 Malaysia Premier League|Premier League]]''' * [[Felda United F.C.|Felda United]] * [[Negeri Sembilan FA|Negeri Sembilan]] {{col-end}} ==Teams== A total of 12 teams compete in the 2014 season which includes the top 10 teams that participated in the [[2013 Liga Super|2013 season]] and champions and runners-up of the [[2013 Liga Premier]].
